SUMMARY AND BACKGROUND
This application is a request for approval of a subdivision plat amendment for
approximately 1.16 acres located on the west side of 900 East, at approximately 12542 S.
900 East (Exhibits B and C). The property is currently zoned RA2. The applicant is
requesting a subdivision plat amendment to subdivide one lot into two lots.

The subject property is Lot 3 of the DeVearl Decker subdivision which was first created in
1994 as a three lot subdivision (Exhibit G). Lot 1 of the DeVearl Decker subdivision was
subdivided in 2018 into two lots now known as the Stewart Acres subdivision. Lot 2 of the
DeVearl Decker subdivision will remain unchanged. The existing home on the subject
property was built in 1899 and will remain on one lot, with the other newly created lot
intended to be developed with a new single-family residence.

According to DCMC Section 9-8-020 the purpose of the RA2 zoning classification is to “foster
low density development with little impact on its surroundings and municipal services; to
generally preserve the character of the City’s semi-rural areas; and to promote and preserve
conditions favorable to large-lot family life, including the keeping of limited numbers of animals
and fowl. The predominant use in these zones is intended to be detached single-family
dwellings, protected from encroachment by commercial and industrial uses.”

The proposed subdivision amendment will create two lots from one existing lot. The lot
numbers for the new plat follow sequentially from the current lot number and will be
known as Lots 4 and 5. The existing home and one accessory structure will remain on Lot 5
and meet all applicable zoning setbacks and standards. Existing accessory buildings will
need to be removed from the area of Lot 4 prior to recordation of the mylar. The proposed
layout of the new lot with a single-family home and accessory structure appear to meet all
setbacks. Zoning compliance for new construction on Lot 4 will be reviewed when a
building permit is submitted.

Criteria For Approval. The grounds for review and potential approval of a subdivision plat
amendment request are found in Section 17-9-050 of the DCMC. This section depicts the
standard of review for such requests as:

        The Planning Commission may approve the vacation or amendment of a plat if the
        Planning Commission finds that there is good cause for the vacation or amendment, and
        no public street or municipal utility easement has been vacated or amended.

STAFF RECOMMENDATION
Staff finds that the application complies with the DCMC and recommends that the Planning
Commission review the request and approve the application based on the findings listed
below and the criteria for approval, as listed within the staff report.

If the Planning Commission decides to approve the request, staff notes the applicant is
required to comply with the following requirements pertaining to the plat and
development of the subdivision:




Victoria 2                                                           App. # 2024-0197-SUB
Subdivision Plat Amendment Request            4
1.      Compliance with all requirements of the Draper City Engineering, Public Works,
        Building, Planning, and Fire Divisions throughout the development of the site and
        the construction of all buildings on the site, including permitting.
2.      All structures on the property that would not be in compliance with zoning
        standards must be removed prior to obtaining the signature of approval from the
        Zoning Administrator on the final plat and prior to the recordation of the mylar.
3.      All requirements of the geotechnical report must be satisfied throughout the
        development of the site and the construction of all buildings on the site.
4.      Approval of a subdivision plat amendment shall be rendered null and void if the plat
        is not recorded within one (1) year from the date of approval or construction of the
        required landscaping and infrastructure has not commenced. This time period may
        be extended by the Planning Commission for up to one additional six (6) month
        period for good cause shown. The subdivider must petition in writing for an
        extension prior to the expiration of the original one (1) year. See DCMC Section 17-
        9-070.
